traceability.notes:
Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS is fully implemented.
Each requirement is satisfied and backed by targeted tests: - REQ-MAINT-DETECT: detectStaleAnnotations implements scanning for @story paths and flags missing story files. Multiple tests cover clean workspaces, stale references, nested directories, non-existent roots, permission errors, and security/path-traversal safeguards. - REQ-MAINT-UPDATE: updateAnnotationReferences performs safe, in-place regex-based updates of @story paths. Tests verify correct updating, no-op behavior when nothing matches, and safe handling of non-existent directories. - REQ-MAINT-BATCH: batchUpdateAnnotations applies multiple mappings (conceptually supporting bulk operations) and is tested to behave correctly when no mappings are given. It also operates across all files under a workspace, satisfying the batch-update intention. - REQ-MAINT-VERIFY: verifyAnnotations wraps detectStaleAnnotations and returns boolean validity; tests confirm true when matching story files exist, and CLI verify uses it to provide user feedback. - REQ-MAINT-REPORT: generateMaintenanceReport renders an empty string when nothing is stale and a newline-separated list when stale annotations are present. Both direct API and CLI reporting behaviors (text and JSON) are tested. - REQ-MAINT-SAFE: Safety is addressed at both API and CLI layers: - Core APIs gracefully handle missing directories, file read failures, and project boundary enforcement. - CLI requires explicit parameters for update, offers dry-run mode, surfaces invalid flag usage with clear error messages, catches unexpected errors, and returns appropriate exit codes (0, 1, 2). Tests explicitly assert these behaviors.
Acceptance criteria are therefore met: - Core Functionality: Detection and update of annotation references (including batch operations and verification) are implemented and exercised in tests and CLI. - Quality Standards: Updates only change the @story path text in comments, preserving surrounding code; writes are conditional on actual content change, avoiding unnecessary rewrites. - Integration: Maintenance helpers are exposed via the plugin’s public API and a dedicated CLI, and reuse existing story validation utilities, aligning with the ESLint plugin’s structure. - User Experience: CLI provides clear commands, messages, JSON outputs for tooling, help text, and explicit error messages; tests assert these UX aspects. - Error Handling: APIs and CLI handle missing roots, permission errors, invalid flags, and unsafe paths without crashing, returning well-defined codes and messages. - Documentation: The README documents the maintenance CLI commands and usage with concrete examples and links to more detailed API/CLI docs.
Given passing tests and clear traceability between code, tests, and the story requirements, this story’s implementation status is PASSED.
